section.title: Solr MCP Codebase Intellectual Property (IP) Clearance Status
Description
section.p: Solr MCP lets you Search, index, and manage Apache Solr collections using natural language — no need to hand-craft Solr queries, build filter expressions, or memorize the admin API using the MCP protocol.

ul.li: Donated by Aditya Parikh via a CLA
Which PMC will be responsible for the code: Apache Solr PMC
Into which existing project/module: Solr MCP — a new sub-project under the Apache Solr umbrella
Officer or member managing donation: Eric Pugh (Apache Member, epugh@apache.org)

p.em: Completed tasks are shown by the completion date (YYYY-MM-dd).

section.title: Copyright

tr.td: Check and make sure that the papers that transfer rights to the ASF have been received. — No Software Grant Agreement is required. All code in the donation is licensed under the Apache License 2.0, which already grants the ASF (and everyone else) the necessary rights to use, modify, and redistribute the software. The upstream project https://github.com/adityamparikh/solr-mcp-server is Apache-2.0.

Check and make sure that the files that have been donated have been updated to reflect the new ASF copyright. — All source files carry an updated SPDX header (SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. A NOTICE file documents the complete attribution chain.

section.p: Identify name recorded for software grant: N/A — No Software Grant Agreement is being filed. All donated code is Apache-2.0 licensed; the Apache-2.0 license itself constitutes sufficient rights transfer. See the repository NOTICE file for the full attribution record.

section.title: Verify distribution rights
section.p: Corporations and individuals holding existing distribution rights:

ul.li: Aditya Parikh — Apache Contributor, ICLA on file

tr.td:
Check and make sure that all items depended upon by the project are covered by one or more of the following approved licenses: Apache, BSD, Artistic, MIT/X, MIT/W3C, MPL 1.1, or something with essentially the same terms. — The direct runtime dependencies of the imported code base, adityamparikh/solr-mcp-server @ cda37f29, as declared in its build.gradle.kts:
org.apache.commons:commons-csv — Apache-2.0
org.apache.solr:solr-solrj — Apache-2.0
org.jspecify:jspecify — Apache-2.0
org.springframework.ai:spring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc — Apache-2.0
org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-actuator — Apache-2.0
org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web — Apache-2.0
All licenses are Category A (Apache-2.0), compatible with the Apache License per ASF policy.

Check that all active committers have a signed CLA on record. — Aditya Parikh (original author of new Solr MCP code) has an ICLA on file. Other committers and contributors are Solr project members with ICLA on file.

Remind active committers that they are responsible for ensuring that a Corporate CLA is recorded if such is required to authorize their contributions under their individual CLA. — Acknowledged. Aditya Parikh contributes as an individual; no CCLA required.

Check and make sure that for all items included with the distribution that are not under the Apache license, we have the right to combine with Apache-licensed code and redistribute. — All files distributed directly in the Solr MCP source tree are Apache-2.0 licensed. No non-Apache files are bundled in the source distribution.
Discussion about how best to accept the code. See https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/LEGAL-716.

section.p: The result of the above checks: the codebase is 100% Apache-2.0.
